sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ready to learn **What is a Computer?**?

Here's what we'll cover:

• Understanding computer hardware and components
• Why this matters for your coding journey
• Hands-on examples you can try

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Think of **What is a Computer?** like building blocks. 

Every great program starts with small, simple pieces. This is one of those essential pieces!

• Start simple, then build up
• Practice makes it click
• Don't worry if it takes time - totally normal!

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: A computer consists of CPU, memory (RAM), storage, and input/output devices
The CPU fetches, decodes, and executes instructions stored in memory
RAM is volatile and fast; storage (HDD/SSD) is persistent and slower
The bus connects and transfers data between hardware components
Input devices (keyboard, mouse) and output devices (monitor, printer) interface with users

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: What is a Computer? - Understanding computer hardware and components. Master basics before advancing. Practice with the examples. Builds foundation for what's next.

questions.question: Which component of a computer is responsible for executing instructions and performing calculations?
questions.explanation: The CPU is the brain of the computer. It fetches instructions from memory and executes them, performing all calculations and logic operations.

questions.question: What is the difference between RAM and storage (hard drive)?
options: RAM is permanent, storage is temporary
RAM is volatile and fast, storage is non-volatile and slower
RAM stores programs, storage stores only files
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile memory that loses data when power is off but provides fast access. Storage (hard drive/SSD) retains data permanently but is slower to access.
